name: Fungal Spores
summary: At the Barrens' oases, Fungal Spores swell within mushrooms along the shores. The waters quicken nearby life, and the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the spores for its alchemy.

sections.title: Vitality of the Oases
sections.body: The Barrens' oases bring unusual life to the dry plains. At the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis, the water does more than ease thirst. It quickens and changes nearby plants and wildlife. Along the damp shores, mushrooms swell with spores that carry the waters' concentrated power and spur growth. Naturalists study the change, while the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the mushrooms for its alchemy.

sections.title: Forsaken Alchemy
sections.body: Apothecaries abroad gather unusual local ingredients for their laboratories and colleagues. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim sends reagents onward, including to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The spores are valuable for brewing potent chemical mixtures. Mysterious forces beneath Kalimdor's soil have altered their natural properties, making them useful to the Forsaken.

faq.answer: Fungal Spores grow in swollen mushrooms along the shores of the Barrens' major oases: the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis.

faq.q: Why are the Forsaken interested in them?
faq.answer: The oasis waters have altered the spores with vibrant life energy. Apothecary Helbrim uses them in potent mixtures for the Royal Apothecary Society and his colleague Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Why do the mushrooms around the oases grow so large?
faq.answer: Unusual life energy in the Barrens' oasis waters changes nearby plants and animals. Fungi along the shores swell with altered spores.
At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim asks adventurers to gather spores for his research.

angles.text: As an undead, you know the Royal Apothecary Society values rare regional ingredients for its research. Kalimdor's altered fungi offer a different choice from Lordaeron's blighted plants.
As a herbalist, you can see how the life-giving waters of the Barrens' oases change the mushrooms growing nearby.
